venue.name: Victoria Bug Zoo
venue.description: The Victoria Bug Zoo is a small indoor zoo of live insects, arachnids and other arthropods at 631 Courtney Street in downtown Victoria, open since 1997. It holds roughly 50 species including giant walking sticks, mantises, scorpions, tarantulas and what it calls Canada's largest ant colony. An educator is in the zoo at all times running a continuous circular tour, and children who join that tour can hold the friendlier animals. Groups of ten or more must be from an institution such as a school, daycare, scout group or sports team, must book and pay online in advance, and must split into groups of twelve or fewer. The zoo also takes bugs out to schools and daycares across the Greater Victoria Region, and rents insect specimen kits to classrooms by the week.

facility_notes.washrooms: The washroom is shared with Nootka Court and is not wheelchair accessible. The men's washroom has the most room to move around in.
facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: There are no large bumps or humps on the floor. Wheelchairs of all kinds, including motorized scooters, can enter and fully turn around.
facility_notes.stroller_accessible: You are welcome to bring in your strollers, but if they are not being used, we ask that you park them in the gift shop.
facility_notes.rain_backup: The whole zoo is indoors and kept at a toasty 25 degrees Celsius, with plenty of coat hooks.
facility_notes.bus_parking: Two city parkades are marked on their parking map and there is street parking around the zoo. City parkades have a few slots for one hour free parking.

restrictions: Those under 13 must be accompanied by someone 16 or older.
Groups of 10 or more must be from an institution, including scouts, schools, daycares and sports teams.
You must be 18 years of age or older to hold the arachnids, and only when they are feeling up to it.
No yelling, running or tapping on the glass.
No food or drinks other than water.
Only service animals can walk around inside the zoo.
Masks are mandatory during accessibility hour for those 5 years old and older, and are free with admission.
venue.seasonal_notes: Due to Victoria being such a tourism based city, our hours changes throughout the year. For the most up to date hours, please check out our instagram! @victoriabugzoo

programs.name: Group visit to the zoo
programs.description: For groups of 10 or more, which must be from an institution such as a school, daycare, scout group or sports team. The cost is general admission prices with a 10 per cent discount, and the whole group must be paid for at once online before arriving. Groups split into lots of 12 or fewer and stagger their entrances by 15 to 30 minutes, with the previous lot out of the zoo before the next goes in. Only one large group is in the zoo at a time. They allow 30 to 60 minutes for each lot of 10 to 12, and a group may need to book several time slots. Daycare groups are asked to bring an extra person above their own ratio. Private tours and birthday parties are no longer offered. They suggest booking two to three months ahead to be sure of availability.
programs.what_children_do: Walk round a small warm room of glass tanks holding about 50 species, then join the educator's continuous tour to hold the friendliest animals, a stick insect or a millipede, in their own hands. Going round on their own takes about 20 minutes and staying with the educator takes about an hour.
programs.our_note: The zoo is tiny, so a class has to go in as lots of 12 with the rest waiting outside. Have somewhere for the waiting children to be. Children can only hold an animal while they are with the educator, so it is worth staying on the tour rather than wandering.
programs.practical_summary: Everything is indoors and warm, wheelchairs and strollers fit, and the washroom is shared with the building next door and is not step free. Nowhere to eat is published and food is not allowed inside, so plan lunch elsewhere and ask about bus parking.
programs.extra_fees_note: General admission is $18 for adults aged 18 to 64, $12 for seniors and students, $8 for ages 5 to 17 and free for ages 4 and under. Groups of 10 or more get 10 per cent off those prices. Indigenous visitors get 15 per cent off general admission in store.
programs.payment_timing: When purchasing tickets, you must pay for everyone at once online. If you do not purchase online, you may not be able to visit.
programs.cancellation_note: A cancelation fee will be charged if you cancel your group booking within 48 hours of the event.
programs.evidence: Cost: General Admission prices plus a 10% discount

programs.name: Bugs come to your classroom
programs.description: An educator brings live animals to a school, summer camp or daycare anywhere in the Greater Victoria Region. They typically bring a millipede, a cockroach, an arachnid and several stick insects. A session runs an hour, and up to three sessions can be booked at one location on the same day. For younger children who will not sit for a full hour they can split the group into two 30 minute sessions instead. The presentation has to happen indoors with all windows and doors shut so the animals can come out, and they say the larger the group, the less animal handling can take place. They list capacity as unlimited. Visits run Monday to Friday between 9am and 5pm, and outside that may cost more. Indigenous groups get 10 per cent off outreach visits.
programs.what_children_do: Sit together in their own room while an educator brings out a millipede, a cockroach, an arachnid and stick insects one at a time, and hold the ones that can be handled.
programs.our_note: The price is for the session rather than for each child, so a full class costs the same as half of one. Ask how much handling your group size will actually get, because they say it drops off as the group grows. For under fives, take the two shorter sittings instead of the hour.
programs.practical_summary: They come to you, so the room and the washrooms are your own. It has to be an indoor room with the windows and doors shut, and there is a mileage charge on top of the session fee.
programs.extra_fees_note: Plus $0.72 per km both ways. An extra session at the same place on the same day is $100 plus tax, up to three a day. Visits outside Monday to Friday 9am to 5pm may cost more.
programs.cancellation_note: A cancelation fee will be charged if you cancel your group booking within 48 hours of the event. For business groups the deposit is not refundable.

programs.name: Insect kit rental for the classroom
programs.description: Kits of preserved specimens set in durable acrylic resin, rented by the week and collected and returned at the zoo. The 27 piece arthropod kit is $75.00 a week. The two smaller kits, What is an Insect and What is an Arthropod, are $25.00 a week each or $35.00 for both. A 10 piece insect orders kit is $40.00 a week. Small add ons such as the fly life cycle or millipede versus centipede are $10.00 each a week, larger ones such as the honeybee or butterfly life cycle are $15.00 each a week. A live metamorphosis add on gives every child in the class a mealworm to keep and costs $15 a class, with deli cups a further $1.00 each if you want them. Every kit comes with information sheets and activity sheets. They ask for a few weeks notice so they can be sure the kit you want is free.
programs.what_children_do: Pick up the mounted specimens and turn them over to look at them from all sides, and work through the activity sheets that come with the kit. With the live add on each child feeds and cares for their own mealworm until it turns into a beetle.
programs.our_note: This is a box you fetch and bring back, not a visit, so count two trips downtown. The mealworm add on runs for weeks rather than an afternoon, which is worth knowing before you say yes to it.
programs.practical_summary: Prices are for the kit for a week, not for each child, and pick up and drop off are at the zoo on Courtney Street. Nothing is published about how many specimens suit which age.
programs.extra_fees_note: Smaller kits are $25.00 a week each or $35.00 for both, the 10 piece insect orders kit is $40.00 a week, small add ons $10.00 each and larger add ons $15.00 each. The live mealworm add on is $15 a class, plus $1.00 a cup if you want the zoo to supply containers.

images.alt: A large glossy beetle with two long curved horns standing on a piece of bark against a blurred green background.
A large green stick insect standing on an open palm, with a second person in a bug print apron reaching a hand towards it and glass tanks of plants behind.
The gift shop, with a coin press machine labelled Penny Pincher Souvenir Coins, shelves of soft toy bugs, boxed kits and a street window painted with insects.

gaps: No youngest or oldest age is published for a group visit, for the outreach visit or for the kits. The only ages on the site are the admission price bands, which are not the same thing.
No coordinates are published anywhere on the site, so the street address needs geocoding before the map and the travel time will work.
Opening hours are given three different ways on their own pages, and they say themselves that the hours change through the year. Nothing is recorded here because none of the pages is dated.
Nowhere for a group to eat is mentioned. Food and drink other than water are not allowed inside the zoo.
Nothing is published about bus parking or a drop off point. The parking page covers two city parkades and street parking only.
How many adults have to come is not given as a ratio. They say each lot of 10 to 12 needs at least one adult, and ask daycare groups to bring one extra person above their own ratio.
There is no published minimum notice for a group visit to the zoo, only a suggestion to book two to three months ahead. The two week minimum applies to the outreach visits.
The teacher discount described on the admissions page is named as the Summer 2025 discount, so it may no longer run.
None of the photographs on the site carries alt text. The descriptions here were written after opening each image in a browser and looking at it.

conflicts.note: Their pages give different opening hours. One says 10 to 5 every day, another says 11 to 4 on weekdays and 10 to 4 at weekends. They also say the hours change through the year, so ring before you fix a departure time.
The masks required quiet hour on Wednesday is listed as 10 to 11 in one place and 11 to 12 in another. If a mask rule matters to your group either way, check which hour it is when you book.
